title: Gel nail polish as an alternative to traditional coverslip sealants
author: Kennedy, Chitsaz, et al.
materials: All procedures with animals were performed in accordance with the Canadian Council on Animal Care guidelines for the use of animals in research. Chicken embryos were incubated at 39 °C until harvesting. Stage 23 chick embryos [3] were fixed by immersion in Carnoy's solution and then embedded in paraffin blocks. Paraffin sections, 12 µm thick, were cut using a microtome onto Superfrost Plus slides (Fisher Scientific, Montreal), dewaxed at 60 °C in an oven, then rehydrated sequentially in xylene, 100% EtOH, 95% EtOH, 70% EtOH, and PBS. Tissue sections were then washed in PBS and blocked in PBS with 5% heat-inactivated horse serum and 0.1% Triton-100X prior to overnight labeling at 4 °C with a mouse anti-Beta tubulin III antibody (TUJ1, 1:1000, BioLegend, San Diego). After washes, the sections were labeled with an anti-mouse Alexa-488 conjugated secondary antibody (1:1000 dilution, Jackson ImmunoResearch Labs, West Grove, PA) and Hoechst 33,342 dye (ThermoFisher) for 1 hour at room temperature (22 °C).

Glass microscope slides were coverslipped using 24×50 mm cover glasses and mounting medium (Fluoromount-G, Invitrogen, Burlington). All excess mounting medium was wiped off the edges of the slides by gently tilting them onto a Kimwipe tissue. The slides were then each sealed using one of three sealing conditions. For each condition, a plastic 200 µl pipette tip with approximately 5 mm cut off its tip was used to pipette the polish onto the edges of the coverslip. All conditions employed the use of clear finishing polishes called top coats. The first condition employed the use of a traditional air-drying top coat (Sally Hansen Complete Salon Manicure Fast Dry Top Coat, Sally Hansen, NY). It was applied and left to dry completely in the dark. In the second and third conditions Top Gelcoat X (Aprés Nail, City of Industry, CA) or Color Gel 001 Jet Black (Leafgel, Toronto, Canada) was used as a sealant and the slides were placed in a gel-curing apparatus under UV light (SUN T5 2-in-1 75 W LED/UV Lamp, China) for 10 or 60 s, respectively. Once cured, the slides were completely dry to the touch. Slides were imaged using a Zeiss Axio Observer widefield microscope (Carl Zeiss Canada, Toronto). The intensity of the 350 nm and 488 nm excited fluorophores was measured using ImageJ [5] to visualize samples and detect bleaching.

Once flat, Extend Gel was applied with its brush onto the gel structure in order to glue down the coverslip. Mounting medium (Fluoromount-G, Invitrogen, Burlington) was dropped into the well formed by the polymerized Extend Gel structure. Adult mouse hippocampal slices (300 µm-thick) were sectioned as described [2], fixed by immersion in 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS, and placed into the mounting medium. A coverslip was then placed over the applied gel on the structure and cured in the lamp for 30 s. This allowed the Extend Gel to solidify completely, adhering the coverslip to the gel structure. Following this, Extend Gel was applied to the edges of the 3D structure in the space between the coverslip and the slide in order to seal any remaining gaps (Fig. 3). The slide was then cured for an additional 30 s, which allowed it to become completely sealed and ready to image.

steps.title: Incubate and fix embryos
steps.instruction: Incubate fertilized chicken eggs at 39 °C until they reach stage 23, then harvest embryos and fix them by immersion in Carnoy’s solution.

steps.title: Embed and section tissue
steps.instruction: Embed the fixed embryos in paraffin blocks and cut 12 µm sections onto Superfrost Plus slides (Fisher Scientific, Montreal).

steps.title: Dewax and rehydrate sections
steps.instruction: Place slides in a 60 °C oven to dewax, then rehydrate sequentially in xylene, 100 % ethanol, 95 % ethanol, 70 % ethanol, and PBS.

steps.title: Block and primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Wash sections in PBS, block in PBS containing 5 % heat‑inactivated horse serum and 0.1 % Triton‑100X, then incubate overnight at 4 °C with mouse anti‑β‑tubulin III (TUJ1, 1:1000, BioLegend, San Diego).

steps.title: Secondary antibody and nuclear stain
steps.instruction: After washes, incubate 1 hour at room temperature (22 °C) with anti‑mouse Alexa‑488 secondary antibody (1:1000, Jackson ImmunoResearch Labs, West Grove, PA) and Hoechst 33342 dye (ThermoFisher).

steps.title: Mount coverslip with Fluoromount‑G
steps.instruction: Add Fluoromount‑G (Invitrogen, Burlington) onto the section, place a 24 × 50 mm cover glass, and gently tilt the slide onto a Kimwipe to remove excess mounting medium from the edges.

steps.title: Seal edges with chosen top coat
steps.instruction: Using a 200 µL plastic pipette tip trimmed ~5 mm from the tip, pipette the selected top‑coat onto the edges of the coverslip. Choose one of the following: (a) Sally Hansen Complete Salon Manicure Fast‑Dry Top Coat – air‑dry in the dark; (b) Top Gelcoat X (Aprés Nail, City of Industry, CA) – UV‑cure for 10 s; (c) Color Gel 001 Jet Black (Leafgel, Toronto, Canada) – UV‑cure for 60 s.

steps.title: Cure gel‑polish (if applicable)
steps.instruction: Place the sealed slide into the SUN T5 2‑in‑1 LED/UV lamp (75 W, China) and cure for the selected time (10, 30, or 60 seconds). A 10‑second cure is sufficient to harden the gel; the slide should feel dry to the touch.

steps.title: Verify lamp emission range
steps.instruction: Confirm that the LED/UV lamp emits predominantly between 365 nm and 405 nm (manufacturer specification).

steps.title: Assess nail polish autofluorescence
steps.instruction: Dispense small spots of nail polish onto a clean microscope slide, cure as above, and image to evaluate any autofluorescence before using the polish on experimental slides.

steps.title: Build Extend Gel layers
steps.instruction: Apply Extend Gel (Aprés Nail) to the edges of a clean coverslip with its brush, forming the first layer of the 3D structure.

steps.title: Cure and ethanol‑wipe each layer
steps.instruction: Cure the applied layer for 30 seconds (or 60 seconds as described), then wipe the surface with 70 % ethanol. Repeat application, cure, and wipe until the desired gel thickness is achieved.

steps.title: Flatten gel wall with 100‑grit file
steps.instruction: Flatten the cured gel wall using a 100‑grit nail file (Nail File 100/180 Grit, Aprés Nail).

steps.title: Glue coverslip with liquid Extend Gel
steps.instruction: Apply a thin layer of liquid Extend Gel onto the flattened surface to adhere the coverslip to the gel structure.

steps.title: Add mounting medium and place coverslip
steps.instruction: Drop Fluoromount‑G into the well created by the polymerized Extend Gel structure. Adult mouse hippocampal slices (300 µm thick) fixed by immersion in 4 % paraformaldehyde in PBS are placed into the mounting medium, then the coverslip is positioned over the gel.

steps.title: Final cure and seal slide
steps.instruction: Cure the assembled slide for 30 seconds under the LED/UV lamp, then apply Extend Gel to the edges of the 3D structure to fill any remaining gaps and cure an additional 30 seconds. The slide is now completely sealed and ready for imaging.

steps.title: Image slides with microscope
steps.instruction: Image the sealed slides using a Zeiss Axio Observer widefield microscope (Carl Zeiss Canada, Toronto) and quantify fluorescence intensity with ImageJ/Fiji.
